In lieu of the sensational over-the-top nature of the editorial, the site it was posted on, the article's writer being a principal of Americans United for Life, and the fact that the first paragraph begins with a bold-faced lie, I'm inclined to throw away the entire article as pure bullshit by a partisan. In point of fact, Planned Parenthood's family planning department does not receive, has never received, and most likely will never receive one penny from the federal government. The only government money they receive is for things like mammograms, which are not only funded separately, but thanks to President Bush, have to actually be separate corporate entities with separate bank accounts.

Just as important, having actually been exposed to the "business" side of organ and tissue donation, I'm here to tell you this isn't news. If you receive a heart transplant, on your insurance bill, there is indeed a line item for remuneration in exchange for the heart. Where I live in Colorado, while the organs are donated, the organization that distributes them actually operates at a profit. If you receive a bone marrow transplant, you better believe that isn't free either. It costs money to harvest organs and tissue, store them in sanitized and stable environments, transport them, etc.

The law against organ sales is to prevent the auctioning off of valuable organs and tissue to the highest bidder, which is illegal. But the people who do the work of the transplants still get paid, just like the doctors and nurses who do the surgery to implant the tissue in the receiving patient.

Is Planned Parenthood "profiting" from the sale? Unlikely, since they're a charity that only breaks even through revenue from donations. Much unlike National Review, which generates a profit, apparently, from peddling lies.

Ingredients:

  • 1/2 cup chopped onion
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • 2 teaspoons butter
  • 10 ounce package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
  • 1/8 teaspoon pepper
  • 6 fat-free flour tortillas (10 inches), warmed
  • 3/4 cup picante sauce, divided
  • 2 cups shredded reduced-fat cheddar cheese

Directions:

  1. In a large skillet, saute onion and garlic in butter until tender. Add spinach and pepper; cook for 2-3 minutes or until heated through.
  2. Place about 3 tablespoonfuls off center on each tortilla; top with 1 tablespoon of picante sauce and 2 tablespoons of cheese. Fold sides and ends over filling and roll up.
  3. Place seam side down in a 13-in. x 9-in. baking dish that has been coated with cooking spray. Top with remaining picante sauce and cheese. Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 20-25 minutes or until sauce is bubbly and cheese is melted.

Makes 6 servings. Nutritional per Serving:

  • 262 calories
  • 9 g fat
  • 25 mg cholesterol
  • 550 mg sodium
  • 31 g carbohydrate
  • 0 fiber
  • 17 g protein
